 Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Devin Vassell, Julian Champagnie and Victor Wembanyama will start Sunday’s game against the Jazz. 
 The Spurs won’t have De’Aaron Fox on Sunday, as he’s been sidelined by a hip injury. Castle and Harper will handle most of the playmaking duties, while Champagnie moves into the starting lineup. 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox (hip) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Fox was on the injury report ahead of Friday’s win over the Warriors with a hip injury, but he started and played 17 minutes. The Spurs’ point guard being added to the injury report late for Sunday’s game is a concern. If Fox can’t play, Julian Champagnie could move into the starting lineup. 
 Stephon Castle 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Stephon Castle recorded 32 points (12-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, one block and five three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Warriors. 
 The Spurs jumped the Stephen Curry-less Warriors immediately, scoring the game’s first 10 points. And Castle led the way, scoring 13 first-quarter points on 5-of-7 shooting. He had one less point than the Warriors did as a team in the period and scored 18 in the first half. Castle shot confidently, and the approach paid off as he finished with his first 30-point game of the season. The Spurs play one more game this week, as they visit the struggling Jazz on Sunday.

 #24 
 De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Devin Vassell and Victor Wembanyama will start Friday’s game against the Warriors. 
 After a two-game absence, Vassell is available for Friday’s game. His return means that Julian Champagnie will come off the bench.

 Devin Vassell (groin) is questionable to play against the Warriors on Friday. 
 Vassell could be back following a two-game absence. Julian Champagnie has been starting in his place and could continue to start, depending on the status of both Vassell and De’Aaron Fox, who is also questionable. 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox (hip) is questionable to play against the Warriors on Friday. 
 Fox could end up missing a game for the first time this season. If that happens, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle would likely see a bump in usage. Devin Vassell has been sidelined but is questionable as well. If he returns and Fox is out, Julian Champagnie will continue to start. If both are out, Keldon Johnson or Carter Bryant could enter the starting lineup. 
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Dylan Harper finished Wednesday’s win over the Bulls with 18 points (7-of-18 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, 10 assists, four steals, one block and two three-pointers. 
 With his father Ron, who won three NBA titles with the Bulls in the mid-90s, in attendance, Harper had another solid showing on Wednesday. The second-year guard recorded his first career double-double, dishing out 10 assists and scoring 18 points. While Harper’s field-goal percentage left a bit to be desired, he didn’t commit a turnover in his 36 minutes. Closing in on top-50 value in nine-cat formats, Harper is currently outperforming his ADP (80). 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox recorded 17 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, nine assists, three steals and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls. 
 Matching his season high in assists, Fox finished Wednesday’s victory one helper shy of a double-double. Add in the steals, and this was a decent night for those rostering the Spurs guard. Fox entered the season with a seventh-round ADP in nine-cat formats, and his production has aligned with that expectation.
